A CPU branch predictor is a hardware mechanism that guesses which way a conditional branch will go before the instruction’s result is fully known. Modern CPUs execute many instructions in parallel through a pipeline, so if the processor had to wait for the exact branch outcome, it would stall and waste cycles. The predictor lets the CPU continue executing the most likely path, and if the guess is wrong, the pipeline is flushed and restarted along the correct path.

Simple predictors track the history of branch outcomes. A basic one-bit predictor remembers
